mentl/97896e6:
Correcting a claim this file carried for an hour. The frontier's standing red
(`why coordinates are the developer's`) was banked this morning with the fix
named as Located(Handle, Reason), a ~157-site change. That is wrong, and the
refutation is the useful half: a handle resolves to its node, but the NODE'S
OWN SPAN IS ALSO A WEAVE COORDINATE, so the conversion survives the change
untouched — it only moves.

Measured: src/parser.mn has no module concept at all. The link concatenates
every module into one blob and parses that; modules are a DRIVER fact applied
afterward from line ranges. So Span(Int,Int,Int,Int) is minted against the
blob and the module — a fact the driver HELD when it built the weave — is
discarded, then re-derived by range scan at every reader. module_seams()
walks the whole span index per call, O(nodes), and three callers already pay
it: the refs facet, the debt lines, the pending list.

show_reason is not a fourth caller waiting to be wired. It is the site that
reveals the scan should not exist. Threading seams into it would add an
O(nodes) walk per rendered Reason node and call the re-derivation fixed.

The ultimate form is a span that is local from birth — the module carried on
the coordinate the parser mints — which DELETES module_seams,
span_render_local and seam_of_line instead of giving them a fourth consumer.
That needs a per-module parse rather than a per-blob one, which is a
link-path change and is where Hβ.driver.link-is-reachability already points.
The peer is DEP-gated there and the gate stays RED meanwhile, because a red
that names a real root is worth more than a green bought with a fourth scan.

Second failure mode, independent of rendering: weave coordinates rot under
editing. An edit above line 8 moves every span below it while handles stay
put, so the resident session inherits this as a correctness problem the
moment a caret moves, not a cosmetic one.

mentl/9741822:
env_lookup resolved a binding by env_find_flat — a backward by-name linear scan
of the flat env buffer, O(n^2) over the compile. env_resolve replaces it with a
4096-bucket str_hash index over the same buffer, returning the latest LIVE
(pos < count) binding in O(1). Byte-identical: a scope_exit can reuse a buffer
position, so a bucket hit is re-validated against entries_buf[pos].name with a
linear fallback for that rare case; name: String on every param so == dispatches
str_eq. dedup_names/dedup_fn_records get their flat-buffer form (O(U^3)->O(U^2)).

Measured: m2==m3 byte-identical (467651 lines), 66/66 micros, 5/5 crown-gate.
HONEST on speed: no measurable change — env_find_flat is ~0.5-4% of the compile
(the diagnosis flagged it as a visible O(n^2), not the dominant cost), and the
run-to-run variance (m2-build swung 1323->1514s) dwarfs it. The dominant cost is
the 4GB never-free cache-hostile image; these O(1) reads compose with that fix
but are not it. Profiling m2 next to pin the real bottleneck.

noodles/9730447:
The builder heard it: a looping progression walked the pad up or
down the octaves, cycle after cycle. Nearest-octave minimal motion
has no register anchor - each transition follows the previous
voicing, drift compounds, and the voicing takes an unanchored
random walk. A gravity penalty cannot fix it (measured: 160
semitones of walk with the penalty on) because every nearest-octave
candidate drifts along with the voicing it follows; you cannot
penalize your way to a candidate that was never offered.

So the candidates are pinned instead: each tone may sit only at
octave placements within nine semitones of the chord's home center,
and the smoothest assignment from the previous voicing is chosen
among those. Common tones still hold (C to Am keeps two, checked),
steps still step, and the register cannot leave home by
construction - the oracle walks the falling-fifths bait forty
cycles and the voicing stays within four semitones of home. Staff,
threads, playback, and previews all share this one function, so
what you see engraved is what you hear again.
noodles/978c285:
Tone's LowpassCombFilter is an AudioWorklet, and its processor's process()
returns !this.disposed — the JS runs on the audio thread forever once the
node is constructed, connected or not. The live mini-verb was four of
them; on a Dimensity 6300 that is four always-burning JS processors no
park could stop (parks disconnect, they don't dispose). The combs are now
native feedback loops — Gain sum, DelayNode (which makes the cycle legal),
lowpass damp, feedback Gain — with the same tunings, damping register, and
feedback. Native nodes truly stop when unreachable, so a parked verb costs
zero, and the live graph now contains no AudioWorklet at all (the crush
color always used a plain WaveShaper; Tone's worklet BitCrusher was
already avoided for going silent offline).

Receipts: dry grades identical to 0.0 dB, wet level-matched to 0.1 dB
(closer than the worklet version's 0.3), phase identical; smoke green.
The full worklet forensics (census, commit bisect, main-thread and graph
audits) is running as a workflow — further fixes follow its findings.
noodles/970d01d:
Even on strong phones the pies and step cursor ran ahead of the ear.
Three defects, one root: the compensation used outputLatency OR
baseLatency, but the ear-delay is their SUM — baseLatency is the
context's own buffering (100-200 ms under latencyHint:playback on
Android) and outputLatency the OS/hardware path. On desktop output
reports 0 so the fallback landed on base and looked fine; on phones
both report and the bigger term got dropped, which is why it was only
wrong on the hardware that matters.

Tone.Draw is gone. A rAF pump now computes the audio time reaching
the ear each frame (currentTime minus the LIVE latency sum — output
latency updates continuously, so a shift frozen at schedule time was
never right) and fires every due visual against that, with half a
frame of anticipation and a stale-drop for hidden-tab backlogs.
Immediate UI feedback (launch/queue state) rides the same pump on the
next frame.

Also stopped burning main-thread time at exactly the wrong moment:
the step event triggered two full grid class sweeps every 16th
(active + queued) even when nothing changed; both now dirty-check.
audio.visualLatency() is exposed for on-device debugging.
